title: A “Perspectival” Mirror of the Elephant: Investigating Language Bias on Google, ChatGPT, YouTube, and Wikipedia
findings: The study found significant language bias across Google, YouTube, Wikipedia, and ChatGPT regarding Buddhism. Search results in different languages present distinct, culturally-specific views rather than a global perspective. For instance, English searches emphasize meditation and philosophy ('Western Buddhism'), while Asian language searches focus on local practices, organizations, and government policies. This bias is more pronounced for narrower, belief-oriented topics. ChatGPT, trained predominantly on English data, defaults to an Anglo-American perspective, presenting it as the normative view and effectively erasing other cultural understandings of Buddhism, regardless of the input language.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured 'language bias' by analyzing the discrepancy in information presented about complex religious topics, primarily Buddhism, across different search languages on platforms like Google, ChatGPT, YouTube, and Wikipedia. It aimed to detect how search results reflect narrow, culturally dominant views tied to the search language rather than a comprehensive global perspective.
